fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. Paul writes, "Finally, brothers, pray for us…" (2 Thessalonians 3:1). The man has a whole letter's worth of things he could ask for, and he asks for prayer. Plain and simple.
I get it, a team might need a lot of things. But Paul doesn't ask for supplies or money in this verse. He says, "Finally, brothers, pray for us…" (2 Thessalonians 3:1). That's the whole ask.

That's it, baker. Paul asks them to pray "…that the word of the Lord may spread quickly and be held in honor…" (2 Thessalonians 3:1). Quickly AND honored. He wants it moving fast and treated with respect.

Nope, nobody is locking this one in a leaders-only cabinet. Paul asks them to pray that the word of the Lord "…may spread quickly and be held in honor…" (2 Thessalonians 3:1). Spreading is the whole point, so it's meant to travel.

True! Paul says the word of the Lord should be held in honor, "…just as it was with you." (2 Thessalonians 3:1). So it was already honored among the Thessalonians. Their own experience is what he compares it to.

I can see why you'd pick it, those are hard things. But Paul doesn't mention either one here. He asks them to pray "…that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men…" (2 Thessalonians 3:2). The only ones named in that verse are people.

Plenty of sea trouble shows up in the Bible, like the shipwreck in Acts 27:41, but not in this verse. Paul writes, "And pray that we may be delivered from wicked and evil men…" (2 Thessalonians 3:2). No boats in sight, friend, just people.

That's right! Paul says, "for not everyone holds to the faith." (2 Thessalonians 3:2). Not everyone. Everyone holding to the faith is the opposite of what the verse says. He's honest that some people don't, and he asks for prayer about the wicked and evil men.

Miracles are a big part of Jesus' story, like the signs John mentions in John 20:30, so I see the guess. But they aren't in this verse. Paul says, "May the Lord direct your hearts into God’s love and Christ’s perseverance." (2 Thessalonians 3:5).
